headline: Mod installs get easier, with Windows sound and movement fixes
summary: Players can install from the signed mod index, resolve dependencies, update with rollback and share their setup (#161); this work had not yet been run on Windows, macOS or Android. Development also fixes diagonal stick movement, Windows sound gaps and underwater visibility on Pokitaru, while adding phone GPU optimisations and contributor inspection tools. Audio replacement (#164), co-op (#166) and the Going Commando native port (#191) remain unmerged; the latter builds and runs but is not yet playable, with ship controls incomplete and most menus untested.
highlights: Windows fixes restore Orxon's electric-barrier strands and correct blue explosion debris on Batalia; Vulkan becomes the default and OpenGL programs are retained (#171, #178, #188).
Enhanced Android uses Arm ASR or no upscaler; its drawer gains motion blur, brightness, texture upscaling and reset controls (#165, #183).

Add to Steam was tested on Linux; Windows and macOS need manual checks, and Flatpak Steam is refused. First starts use fullscreen, overlays scale for 4K and Steam Controllers work without Steam (#184, #177).
Object Viewer and freecam let contributors inspect objects and visibility. Enhanced Vulkan gains Forward+ lights; experimental light editing remains behind a flag disabled by default (#195, #196).
Mod SDK 1.11.0 adds per-mod storage and the current save slot (#172). Crash reports gain local Windows symbols and activity trails; bake logs identify launcher and baker builds (#175, #193, #197).

The day's 138,618 added and 49,327 deleted lines are dominated by the RAC1 import: 111,618 additions and 47,520 deletions (#160). Vulkan checks also get faster and resource failures are handled more safely (#163, #187, #198).
